title: CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF REGIONAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTERS
full_text:
CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF REGIONAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTERS
Annex 2 to the Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases <Newly inserted on June 22, 2023>
(Relating to Article 7 (1))

1. General criteria
(a) A comprehensive medical and surgical care system covering the full range of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases shall be established.
(b) As a regional emergency medical center designated under the Emergency Medical Service Act, the center shall maintain a 24-hour response system for severe and emergency cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
(c) A management system covering the entire continuum, including prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of patients with cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, shall be established.
(d) A cooperative system for cardio-cerebrovascular diseases involving the area served, local medical institutions, local medical associations, and other relevant parties shall be established.
(e) The organization and personnel necessary to implement comprehensive care and management throughout the entire continuum of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases shall be secured on a stable basis.

2. Essential facility and personnel criteria
(a) The center shall have a cardiovascular intensive care unit, a neurological intensive care unit, a cardio-cerebrovascular angiography room, a stroke intensive treatment unit, and an operating room.
(b) Specialists for triage and initial response for emergency cardio-cerebrovascular patients shall be secured.
(c) Specialists in cardiovascular interventional procedures and cerebrovascular interventional procedures shall be secured.
(d) Specialists in cardiac surgery and brain surgery shall be secured.
(e) Educational facilities for cardio-cerebrovascular disease prevention and management and facilities for rehabilitation treatment shall be secured.
(f) Specialists for cardio-cerebrovascular disease prevention and management and rehabilitation treatment shall be secured.
(g) Office space for the operation of the regional center's activities shall be secured.
(h) Personnel responsible for patient registration management, nurses dedicated to education, center operations managers, and administrative personnel shall be secured.

3. Treatment capability criteria
(a) Number of coronary interventions and proportions performed at night, on public holidays, and in emergencies.
(b) Combined number of coronary artery bypass operations, aortic operations, and valve operations.
(c) Number of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) procedures.
(d) Number of cerebrovascular interventions and proportions performed at night, on public holidays, and in emergencies.
(e) Number of intravenous thrombolysis procedures and proportion performed in emergencies.
(f) Number of craniotomies.

Note:
Compliance with the treatment capability criteria shall be assessed by comprehensively considering the quantitative levels of the indicators in each item and qualitative levels, including clinical performance capability.
